doc.title: Frank Wess interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: Early arranging and touring with Josephine Baker
summary: Wess recalls first arrangements in 1940 and his Army band, which toured North Africa with Josephine Baker.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: What about your writing? Were you writing before the Basie band?

Yeah. Well I’ve been writing. I think I did my first commercial arrangement in 1940 I think, for the old entertainer, I don’t know, you probably never heard of Fifi D’Orsay from Canada. I did an arrangement on “Alouette” for her. Years, years, years ago. And I did a couple of things while I was working with Blanche Calloway. Well I was with Blanche at the time, you know, 1940. So that started. And then all in the service I guess for about, oh four years, I had a band. I had a 17 piece band in the service. And we were overseas quite a while, over three years, way over three years. And our band was always the best band, wherever we went, you know. So we ended up being the General’s band, you know, after our first parade that was the order would come out, we were the General’s band. And during that time that’s when we had just come up from West Africa and we went, I mean I was assistant band leader and the band leader and I went down to Special Service, you know, to see what they had for the band. Because we were regular Army. And we found out that there was, they were getting a tour together for Josephine Baker. So we put our name down, and Josephine came out and auditioned the band. And we played a few of our things and she said, “let’s see how you do with my things,” you know so we did that. There was a lull in my life, and then I remember I had to conduct [sounds like] Felic Adiss. So we did that, and she said “you got it.” So we toured all around North Africa with Josephine Baker.
